newsitem.title: UK: Oil majors to introduce uniform tanker inspections.
newsitem.headline: Oil majors to introduce uniform tanker inspections.

text.p: Major oil companies on Wednesday said they are planning a major revision of tanker inspection rules which will bring in uniform guidelines from mid-May.
The Oil Companies International Marine Forum (OCIMF), which represents most of the world's major oil companies, said it would introduce a uniform protocol and report format for vessel inspections.
"Our first objective is the promotion of safety and the prevention of pollution from tankers and at terminals," said OCIMF Chairman Gerhard Kurz.
He added that tanker operators would benefit from a reduced need to complete separate technical questionnaires for individual charterers and other inspecting bodies.
The move is an enhancement of OCIMF's Ship Inspection Report Programme (SIRE), introduced three and a half years ago, he said.
Kurz said the revision of SIRE would significantly increase the availability of detailed technical information about vessels.
"It would benefit operators of vessels by reducing the duplication of ship inspections and the amount of time spent on them," he said.
The revision has been developed by a task force of representatives from the tanker vetting departments of leading oil companies, OCIMF said.
Its key components are separate vessel inspection and vessel particulars questionnaires, known as VIQ and VPQ.

OCIMF said the VIQ addresses ship safety and pollution prevention. Compiled by a ship inspector using a lap-top computer, the report will be electronically transmitted to SIRE and to the ship operator for comments.
The VPQ is completed by the tanker operator and deals with ships' particulars and onboard documents.
Both reports will be available on the SIRE database to programme recipients.

OCIMF was formed in 1970 and has consultative status at the International Maritime Organisation (IMO). SIRE was introduced in November 1993 in order to reduce the duplication of ship inspection reports.
